Fix flashing 500 error when connecting to play.clickhouse.com (#8742)

* fix: skip database_schemas query when connector has errors

Prevent premature database_schemas API calls for connectors that are not yet configured. When a connector resource exists but has errors (e.g., unconfigured after runtimeServiceUnpackEmpty), the sidebar auto-expands it and triggers database_schemas, causing a 500 error.

Now, useListDatabaseSchemas accepts an enabled parameter, and DatabaseExplorer skips the query when the connector has an errorMessage. The error is displayed in the UI instead, and the query will automatically fire once the connector is configured and errors clear.

* fix: prevent querying unconfigured managed connectors

When a managed connector is created without configuration, the
database_schemas query would fire immediately and fail with a 500 error.
This was caused by TanStack Query returning cached data even when the
query is disabled, and the template rendering stale error state.

Fix by:
- Only enabling the database_schemas query when connector has valid config
- Preventing template from rendering cached data when query is disabled
- Showing helpful 'Configure connector' message for unconfigured managed connectors

* prettier

* fix: retry transient 500 errors on AnalyzeConnectors query

When adding a connector on an uninitialized project,
runtimeServiceUnpackEmpty triggers a runtime reset. The SSE
reconnection invalidates all queries, causing AnalyzeConnectors to
fire while the runtime is still initializing. With retry: false
globally, the transient 500 immediately surfaces in the UI. Add
retry logic for server errors so these failures are retried
transparently before displaying an error.

* fix: skip database_schemas query when connector has errors

Prevent premature database_schemas API calls for connectors that are not yet configured. When a connector resource exists but has errors (e.g., unconfigured after runtimeServiceUnpackEmpty), the sidebar auto-expands it and triggers database_schemas, causing a 500 error.

Now, useListDatabaseSchemas accepts an enabled parameter, and DatabaseExplorer skips the query when the connector has an errorMessage. The error is displayed in the UI instead, and the query will automatically fire once the connector is configured and errors clear.

* fix: prevent querying unconfigured managed connectors

When a managed connector is created without configuration, the
database_schemas query would fire immediately and fail with a 500 error.
This was caused by TanStack Query returning cached data even when the
query is disabled, and the template rendering stale error state.

Fix by:
- Only enabling the database_schemas query when connector has valid config
- Preventing template from rendering cached data when query is disabled
- Showing helpful 'Configure connector' message for unconfigured managed connectors

* fix: retry transient 500 errors on AnalyzeConnectors query

When adding a connector on an uninitialized project,
runtimeServiceUnpackEmpty triggers a runtime reset. The SSE
reconnection invalidates all queries, causing AnalyzeConnectors to
fire while the runtime is still initializing. With retry: false
globally, the transient 500 immediately surfaces in the UI. Add
retry logic for server errors so these failures are retried
transparently before displaying an error.

fix(sse): Ensure SSE response is not buffered by reverse proxies (#8795)

Reverse proxies (GitHub Codespaces, Cloudflare, nginx) buffer SSE
responses until the first body bytes arrive. Since we only flushed
headers with no body data, the browser's fetch() stayed pending
indefinitely, keeping the connection in CONNECTING state and the
traffic light stuck on yellow.

Send an SSE comment (:ok) immediately after headers. Comments are
no-ops per the SSE spec and already discarded by our frontend parser.

Closes ENG-1033

fix: allow rill-managed clickhouse connectors to query tables (#8809)

Managed connectors with provision=true were blocked from querying tables
by an isAwaitingConfig guard that checked for dsn/host in the connector
config. However, for rill-managed connectors, the DSN is obtained during
on-demand provisioning in the connection cache—never surfaced to the
frontend. This caused the "Configure connector to browse tables" message
to appear permanently.

Remove the guard. The backend handles provisioning transparently when the
connection is acquired. Query errors are already handled by existing error
states.

Replace tabs + radio hierarchy with a single radio selector offering three
authentication methods:

2. Private Key (Recommended) - SNOWFLAKE_JWT with private key

Replace hardcoded file extension checks and connector-specific logic in
handleFileUpload() with declarative schema properties. Introduce x-file-*
namespace (x-file-accept, x-file-encoding, x-file-extract) to make file
processing declarative and schema-driven.

This eliminates implicit coupling between CredentialsInput UI and
AddDataFormManager's encoding logic. New connectors can specify file handling
purely through schema definitions without modifying manager code.

- Create processFileContent() utility to handle base64/json/raw encoding

btoa() throws if the input contains characters outside the Latin-1 range.

* refactor: restructure Snowflake auth with nested tabs

Replace flat radio + x-visible-if pattern with nested tabs under each
auth method option. Username/Password shows both parameter and DSN tabs,
while Private Key shows parameters directly without tabs.

Structure:
- auth_method (radio) → connection_mode (tabs for password only)
  - Password: parameters | connection string tabs
  - Private Key: parameters directly (no DSN option)

This mirrors the ClickHouse connector pattern and provides better UX
by removing irrelevant options per auth method.

* fix: prevent stale connection_mode from affecting Snowflake auth

When switching from password to private_key auth, the connection_mode
field value (parameters or dsn) persists stale. At submit time,
filterValuesByTabGroups uses that stale value to filter which fields
are included, keeping dsn and deleting parameter fields. This causes
both connection methods to be present, triggering backend validation.

Two-part fix:
1. Add x-visible-if to connection_mode so it clears when switching
2. Skip invisible tab controls in filterValuesByTabGroups so cleared
   values don't wipe their tab children

and getFileAPIPathFromNameAndType. Restore all call sites to use the mapper

preserving auto-save for SQL model files.

before waitForProfiling checks for API responses.

Replace file-path-based isSourceModel check with the runtime's
definedAsSource flag, which precisely identifies sources without
false-positiving on YAML-only models in /models/.

* fix: use pending source imports set instead of definedAsSource flag

Replace the definedAsSource check with a pendingSourceImports set
that the UI registers before writing source files. This avoids false
positives on YAML-only models and eliminates the need for fragile
heuristics. The UI now explicitly tells the watcher which files are
source imports via three entry points: submitAddSourceForm, createSource
(used by LocalSourceUpload and FileDrop), and the watcher clears the

Replace the implicitly coupled `pendingSourceImports` Set and

feat: project status' Tables page (#8604)

* Implement pagination support for model table sizes

The OLAPListTables API returns paginated results with a nextPageToken field.
Previously only the first page was fetched, causing materialized models and
tables on subsequent pages to show as having no size data.

This change replaces the derived store pattern with a readable store that:
- Fetches all pages sequentially for each connector
- Detects nextPageToken in responses and creates follow-up queries
- Accumulates all tables before building the final size map
- Handles loading/error states correctly

This fixes the issue where 5 models were detected but only 2 tables (from the
first page) were returned, causing models like "auction_data_model" to show
"-" instead of their actual size.

* Cache and eagerly subscribe to model size stores for persistent loading

The issue was that useModelTableSizes was creating a new store on every
render when resources changed. If the resources loaded before the queries
completed, the component would be unmounted/remounted, cancelling the queries.

This change:
1. Caches stores by instanceId:connectorArray to prevent recreation
2. Eagerly subscribes to each store to keep queries alive
3. Uses WeakMap to prevent memory leaks from old subscriptions
4. Ensures queries complete even if component re-renders quickly

Now when you refresh the status page, queries stay alive in the background
and complete asynchronously, updating the table when ready.

* Remove store caching to fix refresh showing empty sizes

The store cache was keeping stale subscriptions alive across page refreshes.
When you refreshed the page, the old cached store would be returned even if
the resources had changed or needed fresh data.

This change simplifies the approach:
- Create fresh stores on each useModelTableSizes call
- Let TanStack Query handle result caching (HTTP level)
- Ensure queries always run with latest connector data
- No issues with premature garbage collection

refactor: migrate runtime client from Orval to ConnectRPC with scoped `RuntimeClient` (#8933)

* feat: add RuntimeClient, RuntimeProvider, and ConnectRPC proto gen (Phase 1)

Introduce the foundation for replacing the global mutable `runtime`
store with scoped Svelte context.

- Generate ConnectRPC TypeScript service descriptors for RuntimeService,
  QueryService, and ConnectorService via buf (new buf.gen.runtime.yaml)
- Add RuntimeClient class that encapsulates transport, JWT lifecycle,
  and lazy service client creation
- Add RuntimeProvider component that creates a RuntimeClient, sets it in
  Svelte context, and bridges to the global store for unmigrated consumers
- Add useRuntimeClient() context helper
- Wire RuntimeProvider into web-admin project layout with {#key} on
  host::instanceId for correct re-mounting on project navigation
- Wire RuntimeProvider into web-local root layout
- Extract JWT expiry constants to shared constants.ts

* feat: add TanStack Query hook code generator (Phase 2)

Add a build-time code generator that reads ConnectRPC *_connect.ts
service descriptors and produces TanStack Query hooks for Svelte.

For each unary query method, generates 4 tiers: raw RPC function,
query key factory, query options factory, and convenience createQuery
hook. Mutation methods get 3 tiers: raw function, mutation options,
and createMutation hook.

Output: 59 queries + 28 mutations across QueryService, RuntimeService,
and ConnectorService. Streaming methods (watchFiles, watchResources,
watchLogs, completeStreaming, queryBatch) are skipped.

Generated hooks take RuntimeClient as first argument and inject
instanceId automatically, matching the Phase 1 context architecture.

* feat: update invalidation and query matching for dual key formats (Phase 3)

Update cache invalidation and query matchers to support both the old
URL-path query key format ("/v1/instances/{id}/...") and the new
service/method format ("QueryService", "metricsViewAggregation",
instanceId, request).

This enables incremental migration: as consumers switch from Orval
hooks to v2 generated hooks, both key formats are correctly matched
for invalidation, profiling, metrics view, and component queries.

* fix: resolve type errors in generated query hooks

The generator was producing `PartialMessage<Omit<Request, "instanceId">>`,
but `Omit<...>` strips the `Message<T>` constraint that `PartialMessage`
requires. Fix by swapping to `Omit<PartialMessage<Request>, "instanceId">`.

Also detect at generation time whether each request type actually has an
`instanceId` field; methods like `ListInstances` and `IssueDevJWT` don't
have it and should not receive auto-injection.

* fix: prevent reactive loop in runtime store bridge

When RuntimeProvider calls setRuntime with no JWT (local dev), the
equality check compared authContext ("user") against current.jwt?.authContext
(undefined), always returning false. This caused the store to emit a new
value on every call, triggering an infinite reactive loop:
RuntimeProvider bridge → store update → layout re-render → bridge again.

Fix by treating JWT as unchanged when both old and new JWT are absent,
regardless of authContext.

* feat: add JSON bridge to v2 code generator (Phase 4)

Generated hooks now accept/return Orval-compatible types (V1*) in their
public API, converting to/from proto internally via fromJson/toJson.
This lets consumers switch to v2 hooks without changing their existing
type usage (V1Expression, V1Resource, etc.).

The generator reads the Orval schemas file at generation time to
determine which V1 types exist. Response types always use V1 (100%
coverage). Request types use V1 when available (~25%, POST endpoints)
and fall back to PartialMessage<ProtoType> for GET endpoints.

* feat: add generic TData support to v2 query hooks for select transforms

The generated hooks now accept a TData type parameter (defaulting to the
response type), enabling select transforms that narrow the return type.
This mirrors the Orval pattern and avoids forcing consumers to use
derived stores as workarounds.

* fix: strip undefined values before proto fromJson in JSON bridge

Proto fromJson() rejects undefined field values, but callers may pass
them (e.g., TanStack Query's pageParam starts as undefined, or reactive
props that resolve asynchronously). Orval's HTTP client silently omitted
undefined values; the JSON bridge must do the same.

* fix: emit default values in proto toJson to match gRPC-Gateway output

Proto3 toJson() omits fields with default values (0, "", false) by
default. gRPC-Gateway includes them. This caused missing fields like

* fix: prevent infinite SSE reconnection loop when server closes immediately

immediately (e.g. cloud runtime log endpoint), the retry counter
was reset to 0 on every successful "open" event. This meant
maxRetryAttempts was never reached, causing an infinite reconnection
loop (thousands of requests per minute).

Fix: only reset retryAttempts when the connection was stable (open
for at least 5 seconds). Short-lived connections now count toward
the retry limit and eventually stop with exponential backoff.

* Handle `getFeatureFlags` errors in AI route to prevent 500 page

When `getFeatureFlags` fails (e.g. due to an expired runtime JWT), the
unhandled rejection propagated to SvelteKit's default `handleError`,
which rendered a generic "Internal Error" page. Now the error is caught
and feature flags fall back to defaults, letting the page render.

* Set `receivedAt` on JWT in `fetchProjectDeploymentDetails`

The `JWT` interface requires `receivedAt` for computing token expiry in
`maybeWaitForFreshJWT`. Without it, the expiry calculation produces
`NaN`, which can cause the freshness check to silently misbehave.

* Handle all 401 errors with a user-friendly message

Previously only `"auth token is expired"` got a specific 401 message;
any other 401 fell through to the generic "Sorry, something went wrong!"
fallback. Now all 401s show a clear "Authentication error" message
suggesting a page refresh.

fix: apply org custom domain to embed iframe URLs (#8983)

GetIFrame() was not applying the org's custom domain when constructing
the embed URL, causing embedded dashboards to always expose
ui.rilldata.com in the iframe src. This is a problem for customers who
embed Rill dashboards and want to white-label the vendor URL.

The fix fetches the org and passes its custom domain to the URL builder,
matching the pattern already used in GetDeploymentConfig().

* feat: add TanStack Query hook code generator (Phase 2)

Add a build-time code generator that reads ConnectRPC *_connect.ts
service descriptors and produces TanStack Query hooks for Svelte.

For each unary query method, generates 4 tiers: raw RPC function,
query key factory, query options factory, and convenience createQuery
hook. Mutation methods get 3 tiers: raw function, mutation options,
and createMutation hook.

Output: 59 queries + 28 mutations across QueryService, RuntimeService,
and ConnectorService. Streaming methods (watchFiles, watchResources,
watchLogs, completeStreaming, queryBatch) are skipped.

Generated hooks take RuntimeClient as first argument and inject
instanceId automatically, matching the Phase 1 context architecture.

* feat: update invalidation and query matching for dual key formats (Phase 3)

Update cache invalidation and query matchers to support both the old
URL-path query key format ("/v1/instances/{id}/...") and the new
service/method format ("QueryService", "metricsViewAggregation",
instanceId, request).

This enables incremental migration: as consumers switch from Orval
hooks to v2 generated hooks, both key formats are correctly matched
for invalidation, profiling, metrics view, and component queries.

* fix: resolve type errors in generated query hooks

The generator was producing `PartialMessage<Omit<Request, "instanceId">>`,
but `Omit<...>` strips the `Message<T>` constraint that `PartialMessage`
requires. Fix by swapping to `Omit<PartialMessage<Request>, "instanceId">`.

Also detect at generation time whether each request type actually has an
`instanceId` field; methods like `ListInstances` and `IssueDevJWT` don't
have it and should not receive auto-injection.

* fix: prevent reactive loop in runtime store bridge

When RuntimeProvider calls setRuntime with no JWT (local dev), the
equality check compared authContext ("user") against current.jwt?.authContext
(undefined), always returning false. This caused the store to emit a new
value on every call, triggering an infinite reactive loop:
RuntimeProvider bridge → store update → layout re-render → bridge again.

Fix by treating JWT as unchanged when both old and new JWT are absent,
regardless of authContext.

* feat: add JSON bridge to v2 code generator (Phase 4)

Generated hooks now accept/return Orval-compatible types (V1*) in their
public API, converting to/from proto internally via fromJson/toJson.
This lets consumers switch to v2 hooks without changing their existing
type usage (V1Expression, V1Resource, etc.).

The generator reads the Orval schemas file at generation time to
determine which V1 types exist. Response types always use V1 (100%
coverage). Request types use V1 when available (~25%, POST endpoints)
and fall back to PartialMessage<ProtoType> for GET endpoints.

* feat: add generic TData support to v2 query hooks for select transforms

The generated hooks now accept a TData type parameter (defaulting to the
response type), enabling select transforms that narrow the return type.
This mirrors the Orval pattern and avoids forcing consumers to use
derived stores as workarounds.

* fix: strip undefined values before proto fromJson in JSON bridge

Proto fromJson() rejects undefined field values, but callers may pass
them (e.g., TanStack Query's pageParam starts as undefined, or reactive
props that resolve asynchronously). Orval's HTTP client silently omitted
undefined values; the JSON bridge must do the same.

* fix: emit default values in proto toJson to match gRPC-Gateway output

Proto3 toJson() omits fields with default values (0, "", false) by
default. gRPC-Gateway includes them. This caused missing fields like
low: 0 in histogram bins, breaking D3 scale computations and rendering
blank histograms for columns with data starting near zero.

* fix: deep-strip undefined values in `stripUndefined` for nested request objects

The shallow `stripUndefined` only removed top-level undefined values.
Nested objects like `timeRange: { start: undefined }` passed through
to `fromJson()` which rejects undefined, causing JSON decode errors.

* feat: port request queue to ConnectRPC transport interceptor

Port the two-level heap request queue as a ConnectRPC interceptor.
Maps method names (instead of URLs) to priorities and controls
concurrency via the same architecture as HttpRequestQueue.

* fix: prevent infinite SSE reconnection loop when server closes immediately

When the SSE server opens a connection (200) but closes the stream
immediately (e.g. cloud runtime log endpoint), the retry counter
was reset to 0 on every successful "open" event. This meant
maxRetryAttempts was never reached, causing an infinite reconnection
loop (thousands of requests per minute).

Fix: only reset retryAttempts when the connection was stable (open
for at least 5 seconds). Short-lived connections now count toward
the retry limit and eventually stop with exponential backoff.

fix: reset SSE retry counter on client-initiated pause (#9001)

* fix: reset SSE retry counter on successful connection

The `retryAttempts` counter in `SSEConnectionManager` was never reset
during the normal pause/resume lifecycle. Each auto-close cycle
(triggered after 120s of inactivity) incremented the counter via
`reconnect()`, but `handleCloseEvent` — the only place that resets
it — was skipped because `pause()` sets the status to PAUSED before
the close event fires. After 4 pause/resume cycles, retryAttempts
hit `maxRetryAttempts` (3), the status moved to CLOSED, and the
full-page "Error connecting to runtime" screen appeared.

Fix: reset `retryAttempts` in `handleSuccessfulConnection`, since a
successful connection proves the runtime is reachable.

* fix: move retry reset to pause() to preserve anti-flapping protection

Resetting retryAttempts in handleSuccessfulConnection would cause
infinite reconnection loops when the server flaps (opens then
immediately closes). Instead, reset in pause() — only when the
connection was OPEN and stable (>5s). This preserves the anti-flapping
guard in handleCloseEvent while fixing the accumulation bug.

* fix: simplify — reset retries in heartbeat() instead of pause()

heartbeat() is the only entry point for reconnecting from PAUSED state,
and PAUSED is only reached via intentional pause (auto-close after idle).
Resetting here is simpler than adding a stability check to pause(), and
doesn't touch the failure retry path (handleError/handleCloseEvent →
reconnect) at all.

* fix: correct heartbeat() JSDoc comment

* fix: reset SSE retry counter on client-initiated pause

retryAttempts accumulated across auto-close pause/resume cycles because
pause() bypasses handleCloseEvent (the only reset path). After ~4 idle
cycles, retryAttempts hit maxRetryAttempts and the full-page "Error
connecting to runtime" screen appeared.

Fix: reset retryAttempts in pause(), since an intentional pause is not
a connection failure. Also clarify comments so the two retry-reset sites
(pause for client-initiated, handleCloseEvent for server-initiated)
cross-reference each other.

fix: support dark mode with custom/legacy themes (#9093)

* fix: support dark mode with custom/legacy themes

When custom themes use the legacy format (primaryColorRaw/secondaryColorRaw)
or only define light colors without explicit dark colors, dark mode was broken
because:

1. theme.ts processTheme() returned empty dark colors ({}) for legacy themes,
   causing generateCSS() to emit '--var: unset' which removed theme variables
   in dark mode.
2. theme-manager.ts resolveThemeColors() only fell back to legacy color fields
   in light mode, returning default colors in dark mode.
3. theme-manager.ts resolveThemeObject() only recognized legacy colors in
   light mode, returning undefined for dark mode.

Fixes:
- Generate dark palette from legacy colors using processColors(legacyColors, true)
  which applies createDarkVariation() for proper dark mode colors.
- Allow resolveThemeColors() to fall back to legacy color fields in both modes.
- Allow resolveThemeObject() to recognize legacy colors in both modes.

Resolves ENG-1067

Step 2+3 of Svelte 5 upgrade:
- Rewrite all bits-ui wrapper components for v2 API changes
- Create Svelte 5 Trigger bridge wrappers (asChild → child snippet)
- Migrate Select API: selected → value, onSelectedChange → onValueChange
- Replace cmdk-sv with bits-ui Command components

- Replace `new Component()` / `$set()` / `$destroy()` with `mount()` / `unmount()` / `$state` in

- Use `renderComponent` instead of `flexRender` for custom cell components in PartitionsTable

* Fix floating UI positioning in asChild trigger wrappers

Replace `<span style="display:contents">` with `<div>` in dropdown menu,
popover, tooltip, and context menu trigger wrappers. Elements with
`display:contents` have no bounding rect, causing floating UI to position
dropdowns at (0,0) instead of next to the trigger.

* Migrate Svelte event handlers from `on:click` to `onclick` for Svelte 5 compatibility

In Svelte 5, `on:click` on components no longer dispatches events through
the component tree. This broke all click handlers on bits-ui 2.x wrapper
components (DropdownMenu.Item, CheckboxItem, etc.) because the handlers
silently never fired.

- Replace `on:click={handler}` with `onclick={handler}` across 279 files
- Replace other `on:event` handlers (input, change, keydown, etc.)

- Convert bare event forwarding (`on:click`) to explicit `onclick` props

fix: support dark mode with custom/legacy themes (#9093)

* fix: support dark mode with custom/legacy themes

When custom themes use the legacy format (primaryColorRaw/secondaryColorRaw)
or only define light colors without explicit dark colors, dark mode was broken
because:

1. theme.ts processTheme() returned empty dark colors ({}) for legacy themes,
   causing generateCSS() to emit '--var: unset' which removed theme variables
   in dark mode.
2. theme-manager.ts resolveThemeColors() only fell back to legacy color fields
   in light mode, returning default colors in dark mode.
3. theme-manager.ts resolveThemeObject() only recognized legacy colors in
   light mode, returning undefined for dark mode.

Fixes:
- Generate dark palette from legacy colors using processColors(legacyColors, true)
  which applies createDarkVariation() for proper dark mode colors.
- Allow resolveThemeColors() to fall back to legacy color fields in both modes.
- Allow resolveThemeObject() to recognize legacy colors in both modes.

Resolves ENG-1067

fix: re-mount canvas `CanvasProvider` on breadcrumb navigation so custom themes apply (#9137)

Canvas pages keyed their component tree only on `runtimeClient.instanceId`, which
doesn't change when navigating between canvases in the same project. This meant
breadcrumb navigation reused the old `CanvasProvider` tree and the destination
canvas's theme was never initialised.

Include `canvasName` in the `{#key}` expression (matching the pattern explore pages
already use with `{#key exploreName}`) so the entire provider tree re-mounts on
every canvas switch. Also clear the `themeManager` CSS-variable cache inside
`ThemeProvider` whenever theme CSS changes, preventing stale colour lookups in
chart specs.

Closes [APP-813](https://linear.app/rilldata/issue/APP-813)

fix: inject query priority into proto messages for server-side scheduling (#9208)

* fix: inject query priority into proto messages for server-side scheduling

After the ConnectRPC migration, the queue interceptor only used priority
for client-side request ordering but never set it on the proto message.
The server saw priority 0 (lowest) for all dashboard queries, causing
them to land in the low capacity lane of the DuckDB/ClickHouse
connection semaphore.

The interceptor now injects the method-derived priority into the proto
message before sending, restoring the unified priority behavior of the
old HTTP request queue. Caller-set priorities (e.g. column profile
active/inactive boost) are preserved.

Also adds missing methods to the priority map and bumps
MetricsViewTimeRange(s) to 100 since they gate dashboard rendering.

* fix: resolve TS2345 in request-queue.spec.ts

Cast mock objects to `any` to satisfy ConnectRPC's strict `AnyFn` and
`UnaryRequest` type constraints in test mocks.

* refactor: improve request-queue test readability

Rename variables to clarify the interceptor testing pattern:
run → sendRequest, next → transport, makeRequest → fakeRequest.

fix: inject query priority into proto messages for server-side scheduling (#9208)

* fix: inject query priority into proto messages for server-side scheduling

After the ConnectRPC migration, the queue interceptor only used priority
for client-side request ordering but never set it on the proto message.
The server saw priority 0 (lowest) for all dashboard queries, causing
them to land in the low capacity lane of the DuckDB/ClickHouse
connection semaphore.

The interceptor now injects the method-derived priority into the proto
message before sending, restoring the unified priority behavior of the
old HTTP request queue. Caller-set priorities (e.g. column profile
active/inactive boost) are preserved.

Also adds missing methods to the priority map and bumps
MetricsViewTimeRange(s) to 100 since they gate dashboard rendering.

* fix: resolve TS2345 in request-queue.spec.ts

Cast mock objects to `any` to satisfy ConnectRPC's strict `AnyFn` and
`UnaryRequest` type constraints in test mocks.

* refactor: improve request-queue test readability

Rename variables to clarify the interceptor testing pattern:
run → sendRequest, next → transport, makeRequest → fakeRequest.

sec-vuln: upgrade dependencies (#9227)

* sec-vuln: upgrade dependencies

Fixes
* https://github.com/rilldata/rill/security/dependabot/459
* https://github.com/rilldata/rill/security/dependabot/460
* https://github.com/rilldata/rill/security/dependabot/457
* https://github.com/rilldata/rill/security/dependabot/458
* https://github.com/rilldata/rill/security/dependabot/461

* Update resolvers_test.go

  Root cause: upgrading docker/compose/v5 to v5.1.2 pulled in gotest.tools/v3@v3.5.2 as a new transitive dependency. That library's init() registers flag.Bool("update", ...). Since dependency init() functions run before the importing package's
  variable initializers, gotest.tools registers the flag first, and resolvers_test.go:58's var update = flag.Bool("update", ...) then panics with "flag redefined".

  Fix (runtime/resolvers/resolvers_test.go):
  - Replaced the package-level var update = flag.Bool(...) with an init() that only registers the flag if flag.Lookup("update") == nil (same pattern gotest.tools itself uses)
  - Changed the usage in TestResolvers to look up the flag value via flag.Lookup("update") after flag.Parse() instead of dereferencing a package-level pointer

fix: clear error on any typing so modal doesnt freeze (#9285)

* fix: clear field errors by setting to undefined so validation errors dismiss on input

superForm requires errors to be set to `undefined` rather than deleted for
client-side validation to reclaim the slot. Deleting left errors stuck on

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: use force:true when clearing field errors in add-data form

The previous fix set the error slot to `undefined`, but superForm's default
`updateErrors` merge path leaves the entry as an empty array in some cases,
so the field's error UI kept rendering. Switching to `set(next, { force: true })`
replaces the store value wholesale, which reliably clears the inline error
and re-enables the submit button.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: clear all field errors on any text input change in add-data form

Rather than trying to surgically clear the edited field, reset the whole
errors store on every keystroke. Validation re-runs on submit anyway, so
the remaining errors surface immediately if still present. This sidesteps
superForm's internal error-tree merging, which was keeping stale errors
visible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* debug: log onStringInputChange to diagnose error persistence

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: clear all errors on text input in `AddDataFormStructure`

The previous `clearSubmitErrors` only removed the `submitError` key via
`delete`, but superForm keeps its internal error tree separately — deleting
left per-field errors (like a bad GCS URI) visible and the submit button
disabled even after the user corrected the text.

Replacing the whole errors store with `{}` via `set({}, { force: true })`
bypasses superForm's merge logic so the inline error clears immediately on
keystroke. Validation re-runs on submit, so any still-invalid fields re-
surface at that point.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: use force:true when clearing field errors in add-data form

The previous fix set the error slot to `undefined`, but superForm's default
`updateErrors` merge path leaves the entry as an empty array in some cases,
so the field's error UI kept rendering. Switching to `set(next, { force: true })`
replaces the store value wholesale, which reliably clears the inline error
and re-enables the submit button.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: clear all field errors on any text input change in add-data form

Rather than trying to surgically clear the edited field, reset the whole
errors store on every keystroke. Validation re-runs on submit anyway, so
the remaining errors surface immediately if still present. This sidesteps
superForm's internal error-tree merging, which was keeping stale errors
visible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* debug: log onStringInputChange to diagnose error persistence

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: clear all errors on text input in `AddDataFormStructure`

The previous `clearSubmitErrors` only removed the `submitError` key via
`delete`, but superForm keeps its internal error tree separately — deleting
left per-field errors (like a bad GCS URI) visible and the submit button
disabled even after the user corrected the text.

Replacing the whole errors store with `{}` via `set({}, { force: true })`
bypasses superForm's merge logic so the inline error clears immediately on
keystroke. Validation re-runs on submit, so any still-invalid fields re-
surface at that point.

fix: emit NULL literal for nil values in `SelectInlineResults` (#9336)

* fix: emit NULL literal for nil values in `SelectInlineResults`

BigQuery's Go client rejects nil parameter values in
`bigquery.QueryParameter`. When a metrics aggregation query with
comparison time ranges returns NULL dimension values, `getArgExpr`
was emitting a `?` placeholder with a nil arg, causing
"bigquery: nil parameter" errors.

Emit a SQL `NULL` literal instead and skip appending nil to the
args slice so positional parameter alignment is preserved.

or "merge" terminology. `Publish` auto-commits any local changes with a

* Open `/-/invite` or `/-/deploying` in a new tab on Publish/Merge

Mirror the local Rill Developer deploy/update flow from the cloud editor:
on first deployment open `/-/invite` in a new tab, on subsequent
deployments open `/-/deploying`. Self-managed projects can also lack a
prod deployment (via `rill project connect-github --skip-deploy`), so
`MergePopover` now applies the same first-vs-subsequent logic and gains
the deployments lookup. The current edit tab no longer navigates; the
popover just closes. Drops the cloud-only `source=publish` query param
and the now-orphaned `ProjectPublishing` component.

tab is opened synchronously to `about:blank` and navigated once the

* prettier

* Render `/-/invite` immediately, even when prod is still PENDING

The project layout gates all non-edit routes on the runtime being
RUNNING. When the cloud editor's `Publish` button kicks off a fresh
prod deployment and opens `/-/invite` in a new tab, the deployment is
still PENDING — so the layout was rendering `ProjectBuilding` instead
of the invite page until the deployment finished provisioning. Users
saw a "deploying" spinner *before* the invite page and another
`DashboardBuilding` spinner *after* it (on `/-/deploying`).

Treat `/-/invite` like `/-/edit`: bypass the runtime gate and render
the page immediately with a `SlimProjectHeader`. The invite page only
talks to the admin server, so it doesn't need a live runtime, and
inviting teammates is meant to fill the wait while the deployment
provisions in the background. Also exempt `/-/invite` from
`maybeRedirectToEditableDeployment` for the same reason `/-/deploying`
is exempted — both are transitional pages.

* Use `RedeployProject` to handle dormant prod deployments on Publish/Merge

Previously the popovers detected "first publish" by checking
`ListDeployments` for any deployment with `environment === "prod"`. That
signal is too loose: a project can have a stale prod deployment record
whose project pointer (`prod_deployment_id`) has been cleared, leaving
the layout in the "Your project is hibernating" state. In that case we
were skipping deployment creation, routing to `/-/deploying`, and
landing the user on the hibernating CTA with no way forward.

Switch the routing signal to `GetProject.deployment` (the row pointed
to by `proj.PrimaryDeploymentID` — the same source the project layout
uses), and replace `CreateDeployment` with `RedeployProject`, which
covers both cases in a single RPC: it creates a fresh prod deployment
when none exists and provisions a new one (tearing down the old) when
one does. Three states drive the UX:

  - No prod deployment yet → wake + route to `/-/invite`
  - Prod deployment exists but is dormant (STOPPED/ERRORED) →
    wake + route to `/-/deploying`
  - Prod deployment is active (PENDING/RUNNING/UPDATING) → just merge,
    route to `/-/deploying`

`MergePopover` gains the same `RedeployProject` handling so self-managed
projects created via `rill project connect-github --skip-deploy` and
dormant self-managed projects work too. Popover copy now branches on
all three states.

* Consolidate `Publish` button and skip `about:blank` placeholder

Replace the publish popover with a single button + state-aware tooltip;
route errors through the event bus instead of inline rendering. Open
the new tab directly to `/-/invite` or `/-/deploying` synchronously
in both `PublishPopover` and `MergePopover`; the destination pages
handle their own loading state, so the `about:blank` placeholder is
unnecessary.

Also clarify the hibernated-prod copy on both flows: lead with the
state and use "resume" to match the `Resume branch` CTA on
`BranchDeploymentStopped`.

* Prettier

* Invalidate `gitStatus` on partial-failure paths in `MergePopover`

`gitMerge` calls `commitAll` before any merge work, so `localChanges`
flips on the runtime even when the subsequent merge/push fails. Move
the invalidation into `finally` to mirror `PublishPopover` and keep
the cached gitStatus in sync on both success and failure paths.

this PR was passing them; clear them from all three call sites so the

Wait for prod parser SHA to advance before redirecting from `/-/deploying` (#9403)

* Wait for prod parser SHA to advance before redirecting from `/-/deploying`

After a Publish/Merge on a project with an active prod deployment, the
deploying page would redirect to the dashboard before prod had pulled
the new commit, leaving the user on stale content until they refreshed.
The race is between GitHub's webhook delivery (which triggers the
parser to pull) and the deploying page's first `ListResources` poll.

Capture the prod project parser's `currentCommitSha` in `PublishPopover`
and `MergePopover` (via a new `fetchProdParserCommitSha` helper that
constructs a runtime client for the prod deployment) and pass it
through `buildPostMergeUrl` as a `pre_commit_sha` URL param. The
deploying page's `useDeployingDashboards` now requires the parser to
have advanced past that SHA before redirecting, with a custom
`refetchInterval` that keeps polling while waiting (the existing smart
interval would stop polling whenever nothing was reconciling). A 30 s
timeout fallback redirects with a soft toast if the parser never
advances, covering webhook delivery delays and the rare no-op-merge
case.

Local Rill Developer's Update flow and a `GitStatus` extension to
gate Publish on commits-ahead-of-primary are deferred follow-ups; the
timeout fallback applies to local-initiated deploys as well.

* Drop the timeout fallback on the deploying page

A 30s timeout that redirected with a "Changes may take a moment to
appear" toast was added to handle no-op merges and lost-webhook cases,
but the toast copy was misleading (the changes won't appear if the
push genuinely failed) and a half-measure compared to the proper fix:
real-time per-resource progress on the deploying page. No-op merges
will be prevented at the source by extending `GitStatus` with a
commits-ahead-of-primary signal (deferred follow-up). Lost webhooks
are rare enough to accept the indefinite spinner until the tracker is
built, since closing the tab is more honest than papering over it.

* Self-review nits: URL constants, console.warn, hookify parser SHA fetch

- Use the `DeployingDashboardUrlParam` and `PreCommitShaUrlParam`
  constants in `buildPostMergeUrl` instead of string literals so the
  param keys are defined in one place.
- Log on transport errors inside the parser SHA fetch (was silently
  returning undefined, leaving "I clicked Publish and it still
  redirected to stale content" with no breadcrumb).
- Replace `fetchProdParserCommitSha` (an imperative one-shot that
  required a manual `prodParserShaPrefetched` flag in each popover) with
  a TanStack hook `useParserCommitSha`. Callers now read
  `$parserShaQuery.data` directly and get cache dedup, automatic
  enable/disable, and access to error/loading state if needed later.
  The name drops `Prod` since the helper itself is generic — only the
  callers happen to point it at prod.

* Note why deployment + JWT are read directly rather than via a wrapper

A future reader might wonder why the popovers don't have a dedicated
`useProdRuntimeClient` or `useProdDeployment` hook. Add a short comment
near the parser SHA call explaining the intentional choice — the
popover doesn't make other prod-runtime calls, so a thin wrapper
wouldn't earn its place.

* Refetch parser commit SHA every 5 minutes

Mount-time capture goes stale if the editor sits open for an hour and
another commit reaches primary in the meantime. Refresh in the
background so the cached value the popover reads at click time stays
reasonably current; closes the false-early-redirect window from
"session lifetime" to ≤5 minutes.

* Use Orval's autogenerated query options for the parser SHA fetch

Switch `useParserCommitSha` from a hand-rolled `createQuery` over
`fetchResource` to `useResourceV2`, which wraps Orval's
`getRuntimeServiceGetResourceQueryOptions` directly. Net effects:

- Cache key is now the standard `["RuntimeService", "getResource", ...]`
  shape, so the prod parser resource is deduped with anywhere else that
  queries it (e.g. `useGithubLastSynced`).
- Errors propagate to `$query.error` rather than being swallowed inside
  the queryFn. The popover still falls back to "no `pre_commit_sha`"
  when `data` is undefined; surfacing the error in the query result is
  more honest than a silent `console.warn` for developer-debugging
  purposes.
- `RuntimeClient`'s constructor throws on empty `instanceId`, so the
  hook still has to short-circuit to a disabled placeholder query
  before the project deployment loads.

* Disable "Publish" when there's no local changes

fix: use onCheckedChange instead of onclick on exclude toggle Switch (#9411)

In bits-ui v2, the Switch component internally handles clicks and toggles
its checked state. Passing an onclick handler that also toggles the same
state causes a double-toggle: Svelte 5's fine-grained reactivity propagates
the onclick change through the signal graph before the internal toggle
fires, so the internal toggle reads the already-updated value and flips it
back.

This was already fixed for LeaderboardMeasureNamesDropdown in the Svelte 5
upgrade commit (c318b8fe8), but the same pattern in DimensionFilterFooter
was missed.

Fix: replace onclick with onCheckedChange on the Switch component, and
update the handler to accept the new checked value directly rather than
manually toggling.

Resolves APP-889

Pre-restructure, the cloud /-/edit/ route tree had a single +layout.svelte
that mounted DeveloperChat alongside the slot for all child routes. The
explore subroute then layered DashboardChat on top — both panels rendered.

Restructure to mirror web-local: a (workspace) group for file-editor
routes (mounts DeveloperChat) and a (viz) group for dashboard previews
(mounts DashboardChat in the explore layout). Different layout chains,
at most one chat surface mounts at a time. Welcome and shared chrome
(RuntimeProvider, ProjectHeader, FileAndResourceWatcher,
WelcomeRedirector) stay at the /-/edit/ root.

ProjectHeader now gates the developer chat toggle on
!onMetricsExplorerPage && !onCanvasDashboardPage, and the dashboard
toggle no longer needs the !editContext gate.

Update the route-parity script to use ADMIN_ROOTS=[(workspace), (viz)]
mirroring LOCAL_ROOTS, and drop the now-stale welcome and root +layout.ts

* Complete the (workspace)/(viz) restructure

- Trim /-/edit/+layout.svelte: drop the DeveloperChat and Navigation

  inside FileAndResourceWatcher with WelcomeRedirector ahead of it.

  remove them.

Mirror web-local: when previewing a dashboard inside Cloud Rill
Developer (`/-/edit/(viz)/{explore,canvas}/[name]`), the dashboard
chat surface should be available — same as local viz routes.

- ProjectHeader: detect /-/edit/(viz)/... routes via a new
  `onEditDashboardPreview` boolean. In the editContext block, swap
  the developer toggle for the dashboard toggle when on those
  routes. (`isMetricsExplorerPage`/`isCanvasDashboardPage` only
  match prod routes, so the editor needs its own check.)
- (viz)/canvas/[name]/+page.svelte: mount <DashboardChat
  kind={ResourceKind.Canvas} /> directly in the page, mirroring
  web-local's pattern. The (viz)/explore/[name]/+layout.svelte
  added in the prior commit already covers the explore case.

* Address self-review feedback on AI chat surface split

- Move the edit-dashboard-preview route check from a hardcoded string in
  ProjectHeader into a new `isEditDashboardPreviewPage` helper in
  `nav-utils.ts`, alongside the other route predicates.
- Add explicit `!editContext` gates to the dashboard ChatToggle in the
  explore-page and canvas-page blocks. They were already mutually
  exclusive with the editContext block (because `isMetricsExplorerPage`
  doesn't match `/-/edit/(viz)/...` route IDs), but the exclusivity was
  implicit; making it explicit protects against future broadening of
  those route helpers.
- Make `ConversationManagerOptions` a discriminated union on
  `conversationState`, so `surface` is required at compile time for the
  `browserStorage` branch. Drops the runtime throw.

* Document why welcome/misc routes are out of parity scope

Add a header comment near LOCAL_ROOTS/ADMIN_ROOTS so a reader doesn't have to wonder why web-local's (misc)/welcome and web-admin's /-/edit/welcome are excluded. They're onboarding flows that don't share the editor's component composition, so divergence is expected.

* Fix CI: TS exhaustiveness check in conversation-manager switch

The discriminated-union switch left `options` narrowed to `never` in the
default case, so referencing `options.conversationState` in the throw
triggered TS2339. Replace with `const exhaustive: never = options`,
which preserves the compile-time exhaustiveness guarantee without the
unsafe property access.

* Scope sidebar conversation ID by runtime instance

Adds the runtime `instanceId` to the `BrowserStorageConversationSelector`
storage key (`sidebar-conversation-id-{surface}-{instanceId}`). Previously
the key was scoped by `{surface}-{org}-{project}`, so a stored
conversation ID survived deployment changes and got loaded against a
different runtime than the one that created it — producing
"failed to find session ... driver: not found" after dev hibernation
or redeploy, and across the Publish boundary.

InstanceId already keys the `ConversationManager` singleton, so this
brings the storage key in line with how the manager itself is scoped.

post-merge flow where nothing is deploying. `target_dashboard`
describes intent.

constant, sessionStorage key, helper functions, and local variables.
The `useDeployingDashboards` hook keeps its name since it watches the
deploying state of dashboards; only its parameter is renamed.

fix: read canvas YAML after async work in saveDefaultFilters (#9494)

The previous flow captured the YAML Document before awaiting the
metrics-SQL conversion and then mutated and wrote that same reference.
Any component edit that landed in editorContent during the await was
stranded on a fresh Document, so the write reverted the canvas to a
pre-edit state and the runtime reconciliation deleted the missing
components from the in-memory store.

Collect inputs first, run Promise.all, then read parsedContent and apply
all mutations synchronously before writing. This keeps the
read-modify-write atomic relative to editorContent updates.

* feat: tag support in pivot table sidebar

Adds tag-aware bulk actions to the Explore pivot. The sidebar now has a
dedicated Tags column when the metrics view defines tags on dimensions
or measures, mirroring the Explore dropdown's two-column layout.

Each tag row supports:
- Click to filter the Measures and Dimensions sections to items in that tag
- Drag the tag onto Rows / Columns to bulk-add (dims skipped from Rows)
- Drag onto a contextual Auto-arrange zone (dims to Rows, measures to Columns)
- CMD / Ctrl + Click or + Drop to replace the target zone instead of appending

Replace paths also clean the opposite zone so a dimension never appears
in both rows and columns at once, and append paths skip items already
placed in either zone.

Reuses the existing tag-utils module and hoists the tag index into a new
shared state-manager selector consumed by both the Explore dropdown and
the pivot sidebar. Extracts the CMD/Ctrl modifier store and the
"Filtered by tag" banner into reusable pieces.

* Refresh expired git tokens for managed repos in the runtime

The managed-git credential token (a ~1h GitHub App installation token) is
embedded in the on-disk `origin` remote URL. `repo.Status()` refreshed the token
only in memory and only after expiry, then fetched against the stale on-disk URL,
so once the token expired every GitStatus failed and the toolbar got stuck on
"Git unavailable" until an unrelated pull rewrote the URL.

- `checkHandshake` now writes the refreshed URL to the on-disk `origin` whenever
  credentials rotate, and refreshes ~10m before expiry via `handshakeExpiryBuffer`.
- Add `gitutil.IsAuthError` and `withGitAuthRetry`: on a git auth error, force-refresh
  the handshake and retry once (wired into Status, CommitAndPush, MergeToBranch, pull).
- Frontend: re-poll GitStatus while errored so the toolbar auto-recovers, and turn the
  dead "Git unavailable" button into a click-to-retry control.

[PLAT-492] New billable metrics (#9565)

* emit billable usage metrics for embedded users and API calls

Add three new billable usage metrics on the existing activity ->
billing-reporter -> Orb pipeline:

- external_users / external_anonymous_users: emitted from the admin
  server when an embed token is issued (GetIFrame / GetDeployment /
  GetDeploymentCredentials), rather than per runtime request. The
  downstream metric counts distinct users per period, so token issuance
  is a sufficient and far cheaper signal. External users are identified
  by the same hashed, non-PII subject used in the runtime JWT; anonymous
  embeds by a hash of their attributes. Owner-preview embeds are excluded.
  These are emitted to a dedicated billing events Kafka topic so they
  land in the same events table the runtime writes to.

- api_calls: a counter for programmatic access that is cleanly separable
  from dashboard UI — the custom REST API, each MCP tool call (via MCP
  receiving middleware), and alert/report query execution. Dashboard and
  SDK/CLI gRPC queries share endpoints with user tokens and are not
  counted.

The billing reporter recognizes the new event names (api_calls as a sum
counter; the distinct-user metrics are pre-aggregated as distinct counts
in the metrics project).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Refine canvas PDF export defaults

* Address canvas PDF export review issues

* Add dashboard link to PDF footer

* Address canvas PDF review feedback

* Fix flaky capture PDF test by pinning jsdom environment

capture.spec.ts uses the DOM (document) but is batched with pure-logic
specs in the same directory. Under vitest's parallel forks pool the
jsdom global was intermittently unavailable, causing 'document is not
defined'. Pin the spec to the jsdom environment to make it deterministic.

* Hide off-screen PDF export header until capture

The off-screen canvas PDF export header was always mounted, so its
read-only filter chips duplicated the live filter bar's text and the
'Readonly Filter Chips' aria-label. Off-screen positioning still counts
as visible/queryable to Playwright, so this caused strict-mode
violations in unrelated canvas e2e tests (web-local default-filters,
web-admin bookmarks).

Keep it display:none in normal use (excluded from the a11y tree and
text/label locators) and have capture.ts reveal it only while measuring
and rasterizing.

* Mount canvas PDF export header only during export

The previous display:none approach did not work: Playwright locators
(getByText/getByLabel) and the accessibility tree match elements
regardless of CSS visibility, so the always-mounted off-screen header
still duplicated the live filter bar's text and 'Readonly Filter Chips'
label, failing web-local default-filters and web-admin bookmarks e2e
tests with strict-mode violations.

Gate the header behind a canvasPdfExportActive store so it only exists
in the DOM during an active export (mirroring the ScreenshotContainer
dialog pattern). prepareCanvasForCapture's tick() flushes it into the
DOM before capture reads it.

* Restore component visibility and guard re-entrant PDF export

P2: prepareCanvasForCapture force-set every component's visible store to
true to bypass lazy-load, but never restored it. Since visible gates
component queries, one export left all below-the-fold queries enabled
for the rest of the session, re-running on every filter/time change. It
now returns a restore closure that exportCanvasPdf calls in finally; the
IntersectionObserver keeps observing those components, so lazy-load
still works on later scroll.

P3: the export button shows a spinner via loading but stays clickable
(Button gates onClick on disabled, not loading), and onExport had no
early return, so a double-click could start overlapping exports sharing
one capture header. Add an early return when already exporting.

* Render PDF title and fix export visibility/observer race

P3 (observer race): restoreVisibility set components back to visible=false,
but the IntersectionObserver unobserves a component once it intersects and
visible is otherwise a one-way latch. A component that intersected during
export would end up unobserved AND hidden, so it never lazy-loaded again.
CanvasComponent now re-observes whenever visible transitions back to false:
genuinely on-screen components snap back to true, off-screen ones lazy-load
on later scroll.

P3 (missing title): the exported PDF never rendered the dashboard title;
assemblePdf only set PDF metadata and drew the footer. It now draws the
title as vector text in a band reserved at the top of the first page
(paginate's titleReservePt), matching the design the CanvasPdfExportHeader
comment already described. Long titles are ellipsized to the content width.

* Keep content on the first PDF page under the title band

The title reserve started cursorYPt below the margin, but the
page-advance guards used 'cursorYPt > marginPt' as a proxy for 'this
page already has content'. With the reserve that proxy was always true
on page 0, so a tall first component (or any first row that fits a full
page but not the title band) advanced to page 1 before placing anything,
leaving page 0 with only the title and footer.

Track each page's content-top (pageTopPt) and advance only when content
was actually placed (atPageTop). Slicing is now title-band-aware: the
first slice fills page 0 below the title and the remainder flows onto
later full-height pages. Non-title pagination is unchanged (reserve 0).

* Match export query instance by fixed key index

isCanvasExportQuery scanned the whole query key with .includes(instanceId);
match the instance at its documented position (queryKey[2]) instead, per
the [ServiceName, methodName, instanceId, request] convention in
runtime-client/invalidation.ts. The metrics_sql branch stays unconditional
since its key has no instanceId at a fixed index.

* Address canvas PDF review feedback: keyed export state, theme colors, form rename

- Key canvasPdfExportActive by instance+canvas instead of a global singleton
- Rename ExportPdfOptions to ExportDashboardForm and move its title in
- Pull PDF title/footer colors from theme tokens with RGB fallbacks
- Simplify waitForStore to a boolean waitForStoreValue; poll queries on an
  interval rather than every frame; rename raf to asyncRequestAnimationFrame
- Type-safe simplification of runPdfExport in ShareDashboardPopover

Fix query result cache leaking across security contexts: include full `SecurityClaims` in cache key (#9704)

* Fix query result cache leaking across security contexts

The resolver query cache key only hashed the claims' user attributes,
so requests differing only in additional security rules (e.g. locked
filters on magic auth tokens), permissions, or skipped security checks
produced identical keys and could receive each other's cached results.
Hash the full marshaled SecurityClaims instead, matching the security
engine's own computeCacheKey.

* Exclude UserID from the resolver cache key

The user ID does not affect the resolved security policy: built-in rules
derive user identity from the "id" and "email" user attributes, which
remain part of the key. Excluding it lets requests that resolve to the
same policy share cached results, which helps embed use cases where the
user ID varies per session.

Addresses review feedback from @pjain1.

The local .env then overwrote the variables of the unrelated pre-existing

In the model reconciler's deletion branch, models that had produced output

rows could never be reclaimed, growing the catalog DB on create/delete churn.

parseIsTruthOperation ignored ast.IsTruthExpr.True, so IS FALSE compiled
to the same expression as IS TRUE and IS NOT FALSE to the same as

Also compare against a typed boolean instead of the string 'TRUE',
and include NULL rows in the negated forms (IS NOT TRUE / IS NOT FALSE)

* Apply security row and query filters in metrics view summary

The summary executor built its SQL by hand and never applied the security
policy's row filter or query filter, so dimension example/min/max values
were computed over all rows regardless of row-level security.

  query filter into a WHERE expression for the underlying table.

  the time dimension min/max resolution (the sample window is derived from
  the max timestamp, so it must be filtered too).

  cache key; previously two magic auth tokens with different row filters but
  identical user attributes shared cached results.

  earlier decision on time expressions, min/max timestamps intentionally
  remain unfiltered so they stay metadata-only operations and cache across
  users. Document this on Timestamps. If a user's accessible rows are all
  older than the sample interval, the summary values are null.

  into SecurityFilterSQL and place it with the exported functions.
- Skip hashing the claims' additional rules in the resolver cache key when
  SkipChecks is true. User attributes stay in the key even with SkipChecks
  because they also drive templating ({{ .user }}), e.g. for ManageInstances
  claims and skip_nested_security APIs which carry real user attributes.

fix: leaderboard columns going stale when context is shown for all measures (#9807)

The colgroup, header and rows each decided which context columns to render
by calling a locally declared shouldShowContextColumns(). In Svelte 5
legacy mode such a call only re-evaluates when the identifiers in the
expression change, so the prop it reads is never tracked and the block
goes stale until the component is remounted.

Toggling "show context for all measures" therefore updated the rows (they
remount when the query refetches) but not the colgroup or the header: the
body rendered delta columns the table never declared, measure labels slid
onto the previous measure's delta columns, and the surplus cells collapsed
into overlapping text at the right edge.

Derive the set of measures with context reactively in Leaderboard.svelte
and pass it to the header and rows, so all three stay in sync. Along the
way, fix columnCount, which counted percent-of-total from the sort measure
only, and tableWidth, which only ever counted a single measure's columns.

fix: keep one decimal on line chart Y-axis tick labels (#9806)

The "axis" number formatter used a single [3, 11) magnitude band with
baseMagnitude 0, so any value >= 1000 produced a 4+ digit integer that
failed range validation and fell through to the default path. That path
applies defaultMaxDigitsRight 0, rounding the SI mantissa to a whole
number, so a tick at 1,500,000 rendered as "$2M" instead of "$1.5M".

Split the band into per-magnitude k/M/B bands with their own
baseMagnitude and one decimal, so 1.5M stays "$1.5M" while round values
like 1M and 500k stay clean.

Closes #9805

* fix: chart resize and dynamic y-axis for non-line explore chart types

The explore timeseries area has two renderers: a custom SVG one for the
default/line types, and Vega-Lite for grouped bar, stacked bar and stacked
area. Neither the resize divider nor the dynamic y-axis toggle was wired into
the Vega path.

  `1fr` track's floor is its item's min-content size; the Vega `<canvas>` has
  an intrinsic pixel width, so the column could grow but never shrink past the
  last width Vega drew at. The container therefore never shrank, `contentRect`
  never fired, and the chart never re-rendered smaller.

  `createTDDCartesianSpec` as `zeroBasedOrigin`. The field was previously
  unset, and `builder.ts` emits `zero: false` whenever it is not `true`, so
  every Vega chart was permanently dynamic and bar charts drew from a non-zero
  baseline even with the toggle off.

  `TimeSeriesChart`. With a dynamic axis the domain can exclude zero, putting
  `yScale(0)` outside the clipped plot, which rendered bars as full-height
  slabs and flooded the area fill. `MeasureChartBody` and `MeasureChartTooltip`
  already clamped the same value.

  spread at the call site. svelte-vega compares options key by key with `===`,
  ignoring width and height, so the fresh `tooltip`/`loader`/`config` objects
  made it tear down and re-embed the whole view on every frame of a drag.
  It now resizes the existing view and keeps brush state.

* fix: disable implicit stacking so the dynamic y-axis takes effect

Wiring `zeroBasedOrigin` through to the spec was not enough. Vega-Lite stacks
bar and area marks by default, and a stacked scale derives its domain from the
stack's start/end fields, which always span zero. `scale.zero: false` was
compiled into the Vega spec but had nothing to act on, so the toggle stayed
inert. Compiling the spec confirms it: the domain was
`{fields: ["total_start", "total_end"]}` in both states.

Add `createStackOverride`, which emits `stack: null` when the origin is not
zero-based, and apply it in the grouped bar, stacked bar and area builders. It
is guarded on the absence of a color field: un-stacking a multi-series chart
would overlap its marks rather than stack them, so those stay zero-based.

The single-series bar chart now compiles to `{field: "total_sales"}` with
`zero: false`. Covered by tests that compile all the way down to Vega, since
the `zero` flag alone does not tell you whether the axis is actually dynamic.

fix: canvas dashboards fail to load with non-UTC timezones (#9822)

Canvas built query timestamps with Luxon toISO() on zone-set datetimes,

* fix: tolerantly decode stringified JSON object arguments in MCP tool calls

Some MCP clients (e.g. Claude, see anthropics/claude-code#25865) JSON-encode
object/array-typed sub-fields of tool arguments as strings, which fails the
input schema validation with 'has type "string", want "object"'.

* fix: search only allOf branches when locating property and items schemas in coercion

An anyOf/oneOf branch that omits a property (or items) still accepts it by default,
so a definition found in a single disjunctive branch is not unambiguous and could
rewrite string arguments that were already valid through a permissive branch.
allOf is a conjunction, so its branches remain safe to search.

* fix: derive effective types from allOf branches by intersection in coercion

An object/array constraint wrapped in allOf (e.g. a $ref decorated with a
description) was treated as unknown, blocking coercion and making the allOf

A combinator branch that refs back to its own parent (e.g.

With time comparison on and dimension values selected, the Vega TDD charts

fix: canvas dashboards fail to load with non-UTC timezones (#9822)

Canvas built query timestamps with Luxon toISO() on zone-set datetimes,
producing strings like 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000+09:00. The protobuf JSON
codec used by the v2 runtime client rejects ISO strings that combine
milliseconds with a timezone offset, so every canvas query failed
client-side before reaching the network. Serialize as UTC instead,
matching the existing pattern in explore.

fix: resize Vega explore charts in place instead of re-embedding on every frame (#9859)

* fix: resize Vega explore charts in place instead of re-embedding on every frame

With a dimension comparison active, the explore measure charts are rendered
by Vega. Dragging the divider between the charts and the leaderboards made
svelte-vega tear down and re-embed every view (a full Vega-Lite compile,
parse and render) on each frame: it keeps the previous options in a Svelte
`$state` proxy, so its `===` comparison of nested objects such as `config`
and `tooltip` never passes and its cheap `view.width()` path is unreachable.
With a YTD range at day grain and several dimension values, that was ~570ms
per frame across three charts, which stalled the page and flashed blank or
stale canvases.

`VegaLiteRenderer` now only puts the size into `options` when the options
are (re)built, and applies later size changes straight to the live view with
`view.width()`/`view.height()`; vega-embed applies `options.width` the same
way, so the initial embed is unchanged. The view is also embedded only after
the container has been measured, which removes the extra embed at width 0
on mount. A resize frame now takes ~70ms and keeps the existing canvases.

* fix: drop Vega-Lite's fixed 1px bar gap so dense time-unit bars stay visible

Vega-Lite's `bar.binSpacing` defaults to a 1px gap between bars on binned or
time-unit axes, in addition to the proportional gap from `width: { band: 0.9 }`.
At day grain over a year each bucket is ~1.2px wide, so the 1px gap left ~0.04px

dragging the divider made bars appear and disappear as the bucket width crossed
the threshold.

scales with the bucket width. Bars are now ~1px at that density and low-density
charts keep a 10% gap.

* fix: report whether a runtime is still initializing in `ListResources`

`ListResources` returns 200 with an empty list when security policies deny
every resource, which is what a deny-by-default project does for users who are
entitled to nothing. The frontend read that as "the runtime isn't ready yet"
and polled forever behind a spinner that never resolved.

Add an `initializing` flag to `ListResourcesResponse`, derived from controller
state rather than the returned resources, so it stays meaningful when every
resource is filtered out. `Controller.Initializing` latches: once the initial
parse and reconcile completes it stays false, so a later model refresh does not
make the instance look like it is building again.

Also surface access-denied errors on the canvas and explore embed surfaces,
which previously rendered nothing at all for a denied user.

fix(druid): narrow unnested dimensions to filtered values with MV_FILTER_ONLY / MV_FILTER_REGEX (#9871)

* fix(druid): narrow unnested dimensions to filtered values in GROUP BY

Druid unnests multi-value dimensions implicitly: a filter like
`tags IN ('a')` keeps every row whose array contains 'a', and a GROUP BY
on the dimension then emits every co-occurring value, not just 'a'.

Add an executor rewrite that wraps the grouped expression in
MV_FILTER_ONLY for IN/= filters and MV_FILTER_REGEX for ILIKE filters,
so the group-by emits only the filtered values. The WHERE clause is left
on the raw column, so its index is still used and the query stays
TopN-eligible. Only top-level AND conjuncts on plain-column dimensions
are used; filters under an OR, exclusions, subqueries and expression or
lookup dimensions are left alone.

Gated by two new settings, both default false:
rill.metrics.druid_mvd_filtered_group_by and
rill.metrics.druid_mvd_filtered_search (needs Druid 35+).

Support query attributes in the Databricks OLAP driver (#9852)

* Support query attributes in the Databricks OLAP driver

Databricks was the only OLAP driver that ignored a metrics view's
query_attributes. #8266 wired them into every driver that existed at the time,
but the Databricks OLAP driver landed later in #9255 and was never hooked up, so
the attributes were silently dropped.

Send them as Databricks query tags, which are recorded in the query_tags column
of system.query.history. The driver attaches tags per statement (as a
ConfOverlay on the ExecuteStatement request) rather than per session, so they
remain correct even though connections are pooled and shared between users.
This also avoids depending on the query text: statement_text can be redacted
workspace-wide, in which case a SQL comment would carry nothing.

Query tags are Public Preview and not available on every workspace, and
Databricks fails a statement outright when it doesn't recognise a configuration
rather than ignoring it:

  [CONFIG_NOT_AVAILABLE.WITHOUT_SUGGESTION] Configuration query_tags is not available.

Sending tags unconditionally would therefore break every query of any metrics
view that sets query_attributes on such a workspace. So the first rejection is
detected, the query retried without tags, and the result latched on the
connection so later queries skip tagging altogether.

Bumps databricks-sql-go to v1.14.0. Per-statement query tags
(driverctx.NewContextWithQueryTags) first shipped in v1.11.0, and v1.14.0 is the
newest release before v1.15.0 started requiring the databricks-sql-kernel-bindings
modules, which add ~585MB of prebuilt platform binaries to the module graph
without being reachable from any package we build.

Verified against a live SQL warehouse: a Query() with QueryAttributes set is
recorded in query history as

  [{"key":"rillUserEmail","value":"..."},{"key":"rillProbe","value":"..."}]

and, with the driver patched to send a configuration the workspace rejects,
queries still succeed via the untagged retry.

* feat: resolve AI report time ranges against latest data with `watermark: inherit`

Reports already support `watermark: inherit`, which uses the lowest watermark of the report's refs as the execution time so that `latest` in time range expressions means the latest data rather than the trigger time. databricks: support Lakehouse//RT, auto-detecting the SEA backend (#9879)

* databricks: support Lakehouse//RT, auto-detecting the SEA backend

Lakehouse//RT warehouses only speak the Statement Execution API (SEA) and
reject the Thrift protocol, so Rill (pinned to databricks-sql-go v1.10.0)
could not connect to them at all.

Bump databricks-sql-go v1.10.0 -> v1.15.1 (adds the SEA/kernel backend) and
auto-detect RT: on first connect the connector probes once and, if the
warehouse rejects Thrift, transparently switches to the SEA backend. The
decision is cached and shared by both the OLAP path and the warehouse ingest
path (effectiveDSN), so an RT warehouse works with no configuration. DBSQL
warehouses accept Thrift and are unchanged. A `use_kernel` connector property
(default false) is available as an explicit override.

The SEA backend exports Arrow C Data rather than IPC streams, so the bulk
ingest path in warehouse.go falls back from GetArrowIPCStreams to
GetArrowBatches (re-serialized to a self-contained Arrow IPC stream via the
driver's Arrow v12 writer, which the existing v18 ipc.Reader consumes) when
the driver returns ErrNotSupportedByKernel. The OLAP path already worked over
SEA.

information_schema.Lookup previously JOINed information_schema.tables and
columns; that join forces a shuffle that RT's Photon rejects
(PHOTON_INTERNAL_ERROR, retry unsupported), breaking the schema browser. Split
it into two filtered point-lookups (no shuffle); equivalent on DBSQL.

Adds unit tests for DSN resolution, the RT-detection predicate, and the
useKernel DSN helper, and documents the behavior.

Co-authored-by: Isaac <no-reply@databricks.com>

* databricks: add live Lakehouse//RT OLAP test (disabled by default)

Adds TestOLAP_LakehouseRT, a live integration test that drives the full Rill
Databricks OLAP path against a Lakehouse//RT (Reyden) SQL warehouse over the
auto-detected SEA backend. The connector config passes only the DSN (no
use_kernel), so a passing query proves the Thrift->SEA autodetection end to end.

Because Lakehouse//RT speaks only SEA, the test requires the SEA-via-kernel
backend and carries //go:build databricks_kernel (CGO), excluding it from the
default Thrift-only build and the standard `go test -short ./...` CI job. It is
otherwise gated like the existing Databricks/Snowflake live tests: a leading
t.Skip disables it by default, testmode.Expensive keeps it out of normal runs,
and it needs RILL_RUNTIME_DATABRICKS_RT_TEST_DSN to point at an RT warehouse.

picker listing the project's Skill resources that apply to the analyst,
showing name and description. Picking one writes a
<chat-reference>type="skill" skill="..."</chat-reference> tag into the
